record.original_question: (V. M. Kopytov, N. Ya. Medvedev). A subgroup H of a right-orderable group G is said to be right-relatively convex if it is convex under some right ordering on G. Is the lattice of right-relatively convex subgroups of a right-orderable group always a sublattice of the lattice of its subgroups?

evidence.quote: (V. M. Kopytov, N. Ya. Medvedev). A subgroup H of a right-orderable group G is said to be right-relatively convex if it is convex under some right ordering on G. Is the lattice of right-relatively convex subgroups of a right-orderable group always a sublattice of the lattice of its subgroups?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a group. A right ordering on G is a total order ≤ on the underlying set of G such that for all x, y, z ∈ G, x ≤ y implies xz ≤ yz. The group G is called right-orderable if it admits at least one right ordering. A subset C ⊆ G is convex with respect to a right ordering ≤ if for all a, b ∈ C and all g ∈ G with a ≤ g ≤ b, one has g ∈ C. A subgroup H ≤ G is called right-relatively convex if there exists some right ordering on G with respect to which H is convex.

Let G be a right-orderable group, and let R(G) denote the family of all right-relatively convex subgroups of G, partially ordered by inclusion. It is known that R(G) forms a lattice under its own meet and join operations. Let L(G) denote the lattice of all subgroups of G (under intersection and the subgroup generated by the union).

Question: Is R(G) always a sublattice of L(G)? Equivalently, for any two right-relatively convex subgroups H₁, H₂ of G:
(a) is the intersection H₁ ∩ H₂ right-relatively convex in G, and
(b) is the subgroup ⟨H₁ ∪ H₂⟩ generated by H₁ ∪ H₂ right-relatively convex in G,
so that the meet and join in R(G) coincide respectively with intersection and subgroup-join in L(G)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a new problem in the 2026 update of the Kourovka Notebook of unsolved problems in group theory, attributed to Kopytov and Medvedev. We did not find a published proof or counterexample resolving in full generality whether the lattice of right-relatively convex subgroups of an arbitrary right-orderable group is a sublattice of its full subgroup lattice; partial results exist (e.g., conditions for distributivity and existence of maximal proper right relatively convex normal subgroups in finitely generated cases), but the general question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on relatively convex subgroups in right-orderable groups, indicating ongoing study of their lattice structure.
status_evidence.claim: The lattice-theoretic properties of right-relatively convex subgroups remain a subject of open investigation.

status_evidence.title: Right-Ordered Groups (Kopytov, Medvedev)
status_evidence.snippet: Monograph on right-ordered groups including the system of convex subgroups, by the authors who pose this problem.
status_evidence.claim: The authors who proposed the question have written extensively on convex subgroups of right-orderable groups, where the general sublattice question is not resolved.
